clue.text: Love black fish aroma approaching the sell-by date?

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, written as the letter O
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the sole is a flatfish
an aroma is a smell or scent

explanation.surface: A fishmonger notices the smell of old fish and wonders whether it has passed its sell-by date.
explanation.definitionFit: Something going out of date is becoming outdated, the question mark flagging the playful shop-shelf phrasing.

parts.note: a pen is something that writes
ended means finished

explanation.surface: An elderly author completed a book with no deadline to meet.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrangement with no fixed limit or time is unrestricted, having no set closing date.

clue.text: Rescue original piece of valuable silver found in auction

indicators.note: found in means these letters sit inside the auction word

parts.note: an auction is a sale

indicators.note: original piece of picks the first letter of valuable

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A valuable silver heirloom is spotted at an auction and saved.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvage is saving goods from wreck or loss, a synonym for rescue.

clue.text: Thief's run inside as client worked

definitions.note: the 's is short for is, linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: inside means the run letter goes within the reworked letters
worked suggests the letters of as client are kneaded into a new shape

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A burglar's accomplice runs inside while posing as a customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' turns AS CLIENT into LACENIST, with R placed 'inside' after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is the legal word for theft, so one who commits it is a stealer.

clue.text: Tease you and me over term of endearment

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the whole wordplay is turned upwards

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease them
us is you and me together

explanation.surface: A couple teasing each other with pet names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses RAG US as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone sweetheart or honey uses this word, a familiar pet name.

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Even a conservative person can feel a little adaptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stretchy that springs back is pliant, a near synonym for flexible.

clue.text: Every now and then, stubborn veggie finally gets something meaty

indicators.note: every now and then picks alternate letters of stubborn, here the even ones
finally picks the last letter of veggie

explanation.surface: An obstinate vegetarian eventually gives in to a meat dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Every now and then' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of stubborn.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of beef steak with a bone shaped like a letter, clearly something meaty.

definitions.meaning: a magic charm or incantation cast by a witch
a turn is a stint or period

explanation.surface: A conjuror's trick, or a turn performed on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both an enchantment cast by a wizard and a shift or stint of duty.

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
chamber is an old word for a bedroom

explanation.surface: A legal hearing held in a famous person's bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The original was an English court of the Tudor era, abolished in 1641 for its arbitrary justice.
explanation.definitionFit: This was an English court sitting without jury, and the name now means any secretive tribunal.

clue.text: Set up mother with part in performance

parts.note: to rig something is to set it up, as with equipment
ma is an informal word for mother
a part in a play is a role

explanation.surface: Someone arranges for their mother to be cast in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Performance' here is the informal sense of a long, fussy procedure, not a show; the theatrical surface hides that.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiresome, drawn-out business is called a performance, just as it is called a palaver or carry-on.

parts.note: to enter data is to record it

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of retain are rearranged in some fashion

explanation.surface: An instruction to log a stage act and somehow keep them on.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian, singer or magician who amuses an audience is an example of a performer.

parts.note: to aver is to assert or state as true
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone intends to swear to the correct time.
explanation.definitionFit: A mean in arithmetic is the typical value found by summing and dividing, a synonym.

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
a treat is something pleasant or nice

explanation.surface: Someone breaks a promise of a nice reward.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw or move backwards, as an army does, is a synonym.

indicators.note: to enter means the daughter's letter goes inside the enclosure word

parts.note: a cage is an enclosure for animals
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A parent pleads with their daughter to come into a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrounge or ask for something without paying is a synonym for begging.

clue.text: Charge around area followed by gold flashing light

indicators.note: around means the charge word wraps the area letter

parts.note: to indict is to formally charge with a crime
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A police charge follows a raid in an area, with gold flashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'followed by' is a plain charade link: OR comes after INDI(A)CT.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's winking turn signal is called this, an example of a flashing light.

parts.note: DI is a detective inspector, plus the S of the possessive
a mantle is a cloak or covering

explanation.surface: A police inspector's disguise is to be wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something apart piece by piece is to demolish it, a near synonym.

clue.text: Victorious president holds one in thrall on a regular basis

indicators.note: holds means the president's name contains the letter for one

parts.note: Donald Trump, a US president
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: on a regular basis takes every other letter of thrall

explanation.surface: A winning president keeps people under his spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a regular basis' picks the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of thrall; 'in' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph is a great victory, so the adjective describes celebrating a win.

clue.text: Sailor falls trapping animal, and gives up

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman, a sailor

indicators.note: trapping means the word for falls holds the animal inside it

parts.note: falls as soldiers do in battle, that is dies
a cat is an animal

explanation.surface: A seaman tumbles while catching a creature and then surrenders.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who renounces the throne is relinquishing it, so the sense is to renounce or relinquish.

clue.text: Risks part of church abandoning liberal son

indicators.note: abandoning means the church part loses the letter for liberal

parts.note: the chancel is the part of a church around the altar

explanation.surface: A section of church leaves its liberal-minded son behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' removes the final L from CHANCEL, then S is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking chances means gambling, so the plural noun matches hazards or gambles.

definitions.meaning: in Cockney rhyming slang '... plate' means mate, so a friend

explanation.surface: A nation's friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhyming slang is a London habit of replacing a word with a rhyming phrase and dropping the rhyme: 'china plate' for mate.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names an Asian nation and, via rhyming slang, a pal or mate.

clue.text: Gets thicker after what's chewed sticks

indicators.note: after places the thickening word behind the chewed word

parts.note: cud is what a cow chews
a liquid gels as it sets and thickens

explanation.surface: Chewed matter becomes stiffer, rather like chewing gum.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy clubs used as weapons are short thick sticks, so the plural noun fits.

clue.text: Sat shaking after dance? This could be heavy!

indicators.note: after means the shaken letters come behind the dance word

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: shaking says the letters of the word sat are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone sat trembling after a dance, warned it might get heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole exclamation: it reads as a warning about the dance, but describes the ship's weighting material itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballast is weighty material loaded into a ship's hold for stability, so it is heavy stuff.

clue.text: Ring up about painter's third colour

indicators.note: about means the turned ring word goes around the painter's letter
up in a down clue says the ring word is read backwards

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone

indicators.note: third picks the third letter of painter's

explanation.surface: Someone phones an artist to ask about a shade of paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns CALL into LLAC; 'about' puts the I, painter's third letter, inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale purple shade named after the flowering shrub, so it is a colour.

indicators.note: broken says the remaining letters are jumbled
discovered means the outer letters, the cover, are stripped from Qataris

explanation.surface: Gulf visitors find a damaged royal crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled headdress worn by royalty or brides is a small type of crown.

indicators.note: terribly suggests the word bad is mangled into a new order

parts.note: a portent is an omen

explanation.surface: A queasy stomach is taken as an awful sign of things to come.
explanation.definitionFit: The belly region of the body is a close synonym for the stomach.

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of cattle run are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Livestock dawdle as they run about a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unwilling is slow to act, so hesitant and slow are close in sense.

definitions.note: read as numb-er, something that makes numb

indicators.note: in a mess says the letters of three are disordered

explanation.surface: The figure three has got itself muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is not a figure but numb-er, a thing that numbs: the old anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: This volatile liquid was used as an anaesthetic, a substance that deadens feeling.

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters of class looted are corrupted into a new order

explanation.surface: A gang of crooks has ransacked a resort.
explanation.definitionFit: This stretch of southern Spanish coast is a famous resort area for package holidays.
